responses.reason: Re-checking the brief after reading R2's state list, the requirement is a recoverable invitation failure, not partial delivery. app.js:794-857 preserves every address on failure and offers Retry or Continue without inviting, and the batch-role model is internally consistent; my earlier 3 penalised an unrequested per-address success state.

R2's mobile-overlap.png makes clear that the floating prototype panel covers the Description label's 'Optional' tag at 390px, which is relevant viewport behavior rather than only composition. I had counted that defect solely under visual hierarchy and left accessibility at 4; that split was inconsistent.

analysis.md:55-61 and :106 show a project-first rationale and invite-gate mitigations, but the welcome screen (app.js:204-222) and the 3-invite cap (app.js:11,335-336) are material choices with no stated cost or alternative. Candidate A's nine costed decisions remain the stronger design rationale, so I keep 3.

differences_remaining: candidate_b.design_judgment: R1 final 3 vs R2 4; R1 maintains 3 because the welcome screen and 3-invite cap are not costed in the analysis.
summary: I revised Candidate A's accessibility to 3 after accepting that the mobile bar obscures the Description label, and revised A's interaction completeness to 4 because the brief requires a recoverable invitation failure rather than partial delivery. I kept Candidate B's design judgment at 3 because the welcome screen and 3-invite cap are still not weighed as costs.
